title: Calculator with Functions
story: You're tired of doing mental math every time you split a dinner bill or calculate a tip. Time to build your own modular calculator — one function per operation, forever reusable.
why: Wrapping each arithmetic operation in its own function creates a calculator where every button is a clean, independent piece of logic.
analogy: A calculator's keypad has separate buttons for +, -, x, and /. Each button is like a function — press it, give it two numbers, get a result. The buttons are independent; replacing the multiply button doesn't break the add button.
try_it: Add a fifth function `modulus(a, b)` that returns the remainder of a divided by b, and test it with different number pairs.
tips: Give each function exactly one arithmetic job
Handle edge cases inside the function — like divide by zero
Use the same parameter names (a, b) across similar functions for consistency
Call the functions with descriptive variable names: `let sum = add(x, y);`
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle division by zero — your program will crash
Mixing up parameter order: `subtract(b, a)` instead of `subtract(a, b)`
Not returning a value from a function that declares a return type
